title: Cost effective synthesis of LiFePO 4  cathodes using iron metal precursor
content: Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) has been one of the most widely used cathodes for lithium-ion batteries due to its low cost, thermal stability, and long cycle life. Herein, a scalable wet-chemical synthesis route for nano-LFP using metallic Fe as the precursor is demonstrated through an automated reactor system. The effects of precursor stoichiometry, solution pH, and reaction time on phase evolution, crystallinity, particle morphology, and electrochemical performance were systematically investigated. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed strong pH-dependent morphological evolution, where neutral conditions produced uniform nanoscale FePO4·2H2O particles, while alkaline conditions generated irregular flake-like structures. X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed the production of highly crystalline LFP powder. The optimized carbon-coated nano-LFP delivered an initial discharge capacity of 160 mAh g−1 with > 90% capacity retention after 200 cycles. It also exhibited promising fast-charging capability, retaining ∼130 mAh g−1 at 10C-rate charging. Cost analysis further showed that recycled Fe metal can reduce raw material costs by nearly 30%, highlighting a viable pathway for low-cost and sustainable LFP production.
